facts.raw_span: pruritic, pink scaling plaques on her face and neck
lesions subsequently involved her chest, abdomen, and back and flared with sun exposure
Well-demarcated plaques with an overlying scale crust occurring in a photodistributed pattern on the central face, with involvement of chest, abdomen, and back
Antinuclear antibody titers positive at 1:640
Lymphopenia present
Normocytic anemia present
Epidermal acanthosis, spongiosis, and acantholytic keratinocytes
Dense lymphoplasmacellular infiltrate in the dermis, with scattered neutrophils and eosinophils
Granular and linear deposition of IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone and abundant intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 in the upper two-thirds of the epidermis
Negative or within normal limits: antiribonucleoprotein, antihistone, antiphospholipid, anti-Smith, anti-Ro/Sjögren syndrome antigen A, and anti-La/Sjögren syndrome antigen B antibodies
Normal C3, C4, CH50, rapid plasma reagin, and creatinine levels
Normal erythrocyte sedimentation rate

rationales.F01: Pruritic, pink scaling plaques are common in various skin conditions, but the presence of these symptoms, especially on sun-exposed areas, can be indicative of lupus erythematosus or other autoimmune diseases.
rationales.F02: Lesions that flare with sun exposure are characteristic of subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus and polymorphic light eruption, making this finding particularly relevant for distinguishing between these conditions.
rationales.F04: High antinuclear antibody titers are a hallmark of systemic lupus erythematosus, significantly increasing the likelihood of this diagnosis.
rationales.F09: The presence of granular and linear deposition of IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone, along with intercellular deposition in the epidermis, is highly suggestive of lupus erythematosus, particularly the systemic form.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation of pruritic, pink scaling plaques in a photodistributed pattern, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal acanthosis, spongiosis, and acantholytic keratinocytes, and the presence of antinuclear antibody titers, supports the diagnosis of Subacute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus.
